questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I've always wanted to go to Australia and I thought: "What better way than to actually live there?"

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I would go on exchange and also on exchange in Sydney a thousand times again. I can highly recommend it to everybody.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: University of Sydney is very informative university and provided us students with all necessary information.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: At University of Sydney they provide Intro to Sydney sessions, Official Welcome session, Welcome fest, Scavenger Hunt and Campus Race on campus so that the students are fully prepared for a life in Sydney and at campus.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: There's so much information given that you almost drawn in it.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Abercrombie Student Accommodation, Darlington House, The Regiment, Queen Mary Building, Camden Campus, Kingswood Accommodation, and UniLodge Kensington.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: I stayed at Queen Mary Building where we had a huge kitchen available for cooking your own food 24/7.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: If you stay at the same accommodation as your friends, it's really nice to know that they are never too far away. But if you come alone, it can be harder to make friends, since the accommodation houses several hundreds of students. Queen Mary Building houses 800 students and was not that great at hosting events in the beginning so people in same corridors stayed strangers throughout the whole semester.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: If you find your friends other places than your accommodation, it can be quite nice to have your accommodation as your safe zone.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer:
USYD has a shared Google Sheets showing all the units (courses), what semester they're available, amount of Credit points, and links to the University's website where you can read more about the content of each unit, prerequisites, prohibitions and so on.
After deciding your units (pick more than you need since they can be turned down by USYD) you apply for enrollment on their Sydney Student Portal. On this portal you check the approval of the units. When units have been approved, you can choose to enroll or to decline.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Students stay in close contact with the organization Sydney Global Mobility, where a exchange coordinator is at your service to help with all kinds of questions.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I had two units declined because i didn't meet the prerequisites. I then found two new units and was enrolled in all four units I wanted. One of the units needed some evidence of my skills in a laboratory which made the enrollment a bit prolonged.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Apply for more units than you need. If some of them are declined then the process gets a bit longer because the new units you add have to be added manually by the exchange coordinator who is already very busy answering other mails.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Every professor at every unit I had at USYD is very good with sharing information. We even got weekly letters from the teachers telling us what we needed to be aware of in the incoming week.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer:
My elective units in Diet and nutrition for health and sport and Learning in outdoor education were very easy.
My limited elective units in Neuroscience and Biochemistry in human diseases were more comparable with the level of my home university UCPH. But the exams were much easier.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The teachers are really eager for you to understand the content and always make a great effort by sending out a lot of information on a weekly basis, which actually turned out to be even more confusing.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Diet and nutrition for health and sport, Learning in outdoor education, Neuroscience, and Biochemistry in human diseases

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Every exchange student should enroll in Learning in outdoor education. It's a unit where you go on field trips to Royal National Park and Blue Mountains. There's no exam, but instead 4 blog posts that needs to be written and a media campaign to be presented.

Diet and nutrition for health and sport is a very easy unit where you learn a lot about nutrition. There's no final exam, but three quizzes throughout the semester and a final report.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer:
Accommodation and grocery shopping were more expensive than expected.
Public transport was cheaper than expected.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer:
USYD has so many societies and a student union that host events almost everyday.
The student union (USU) even offers free food (Foodhub) Mon-Fri every week.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
Endless.
Find them all on USU's website:
https://usu.edu.au/
And Sydney Uni Sport's website:
https://susf.com.au/

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I can recommend yoga which is really relaxing for a stressed out student.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Travel!

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy. Sydney is very busy, but so is Copenhagen.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Sign up for the Mates Abroad Program.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: European students and Asian students don't really mix up, but instead stay separated.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Everybody is always ready to chat.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Don't hesitate – I myself was in doubt right until i boarded the plane, but exchange is the best thing that I've ever done (and I've done a lot of stuff already).
2. Ask when in doubt – The process is long and sometimes confusing. Ask for help if you know any who has been to the same uni or get in touch with other exchange students who are going.
3. Be patient – Response times are long and the time differences doesn't make it any easier, but I promise you that all your patience will pay off, and when you arrive, it will seem to be the easiest thing ever to move to a foreign country!

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Attend the Scavenger Hunt and Campus Race (provided by USU). Here you get to know campus and meet a lot of other exchange students who have also just arrived.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Passing my final exams and acknowledging than I'm actually also quite intelligent in a foreign country.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Balancing studies, social life and time to recover.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Just do it.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
